title: Dress, cell-phone, surveillance notice and general work rules - 2025 handbook
summary: 2025 handbook expectations for employee appearance by role, cell-phone/communication-device use, telephone/video surveillance notice, general work rules and serious violations.

claims.claim: Dress and grooming must be appropriate to the work situation and governed by safety, comfort and professional-image requirements; professional dress is required for scheduled meetings.

Office casual-business attire must be practical, non-distracting and non-offensive; the handbook prohibits clothing that exposes specified body areas or bears words/terms/pictures and provides role-specific clothing/safety expectations for office, drivers, garage, dispatch, cafeteria and custodial staff.

evidence.page_or_section: printed pages 27-30 - Dress Code role guidelines

claims.claim: Employees needing a dress-code exception for medical, religious, ethnic or other unique personal circumstances are instructed to consult their supervisor.
Repeated dress-code noncompliance can result in progressive discipline; employees may be sent home to change and are not compensated for work time missed because of failure to comply.

RTEC's cell-phone policy applies to all employees and is intended to maintain a safe, customer-focused work environment free of unnecessary distraction from personal cell phones and other communication devices; the company reserves the right to modify/update the policy.

evidence.page_or_section: printed page 31 - Cell Phone Use Policy

claims.claim: The handbook states RTEC may conduct telephone and video surveillance of portions of its premises for safety/security purposes.

evidence.page_or_section: printed page 31 - Telephone and Video Surveillance Policy
evidence.note: Detailed vehicle/property audio-video rules are modeled separately.

claims.claim: General work rules require regular attendance, timely reporting of absences, punctuality, safety-rule compliance, proper job performance, immediate incident/accident reporting, staying at the assigned work station unless authorized, accurate time records, proper personnel-record updates and proper use of bulletin boards/equipment.

Personal use of company telephones, communications and equipment is restricted; personal calls should be limited to emergencies and personal cell phones are limited to break/lunch periods under the work-rule language.

evidence.note: Standalone computer-use policy provides additional electronic-media rules.

claims.claim: The handbook identifies serious violations that may result in job loss, including safety endangerment, insubordination, theft, unauthorized political activity beyond voting/private opinion, abusive/threatening language or fighting, falsification, drugs/alcohol, weapons, harassment, leaving work early/walking off, confidentiality breaches, unauthorized outside employment, accident-reporting failures and other listed misconduct.

evidence.note: This is a source inventory, not an independent judgment about legal enforceability.

trigger: Daily workplace conduct, appearance, communication-device use or policy violation.
steps: Use communications/equipment only within permitted boundaries.
Follow general work rules and report incidents/changes promptly.
Escalate exception requests or unclear attire to the supervisor.
decisions: Whether a work-rule violation warrants corrective action
deadlines: Employees are expected to report absences with advance notice and update personnel information promptly.
exceptions: Dress exceptions may be considered for medical, religious, ethnic or other unique personal circumstances.
controls: Company right to modify cell-phone policy
unresolved_questions: Extract the complete cell-phone operational restrictions if a standalone cell-phone policy exists outside the handbook.
automation_candidates: Employee-change notification workflow for personnel-record updates.
Incident/work-rule intake checklist linked to discipline records.
